stemMd: A population grows rapidly when small, then slows as it approaches a stable size under unchanged conditions. Which explanation is most consistent with logistic growth?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Density-dependent limits increasingly reduce net population growth.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Resources necessarily become unlimited at high density.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Births must become impossible after the first generation.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Population growth must be independent of crowding.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The carrying capacity must increase without limit.

explanationMd: At low density, resources may permit rapid growth. As population size approaches carrying capacity, competition and other density-dependent factors reduce net growth. A stable population can still have births and deaths; stability means their effects approximately balance.

distractorRationale.c: Logistic growth can stabilize with ongoing births and deaths.
distractorRationale.e: A stable size under unchanged conditions suggests a finite carrying capacity.
distractorRationale.b: Resource limitation commonly becomes more important at high density.
distractorRationale.d: Logistic growth specifically includes a density-dependent slowing.
